pages.caption: Once upon a time there lived a king who was deeply in love with a princess, but she could not marry anyone, because she was under an enchantment.
pages.description: [A king kneeling before a shimmering fairy]
pages.scene: A king kneeling before a shimmering fairy

pages.caption: So the King set out to seek a fairy, and asked what he could do to win the Princess's love.
pages.description: [The king walking through a magical forest]
pages.scene: The king walking through a magical forest

pages.caption: The Fairy said to him: "You know that the Princess has a great cat which she is very fond of. Whoever is clever enough to tread on that cat's tail is the man she is destined to marry."
pages.description: [A fairy with twinkling eyes speaking to the king]
pages.scene: A fairy with twinkling eyes speaking to the king

pages.caption: The King said to himself that this would not be very difficult, and he left the Fairy, determined to grind the cat's tail to powder rather than not tread on it at all.
pages.description: [The king grinning with determination]
pages.scene: The king grinning with determination

pages.caption: You may imagine that it was not long before he went to see the Princess, and puss, as usual, marched in before him, arching his back.
pages.description: [A grand palace entrance with a proud cat arching its back]
pages.scene: A grand palace entrance with a proud cat arching its back

pages.caption: The King took a long step, and quite thought he had the tail under his foot, but the cat turned round so sharply that he only trod on air.
pages.description: [The king lunging forward as a cat twists away]
pages.scene: The king lunging forward as a cat twists away

pages.caption: And so it went on for eight days, till the King began to think that this fatal tail must be full of quicksilver--it was never still for a moment.
pages.description: [Eight days passing in a montage of failed attempts]
pages.scene: Eight days passing in a montage of failed attempts

pages.caption: At last, however, he was lucky enough to come upon puss fast asleep and with his tail conveniently spread out.
pages.description: [A sleeping cat with its tail stretched out]
pages.scene: A sleeping cat with its tail stretched out

pages.caption: So the King, without losing a moment, set his foot upon it heavily.
pages.description: [The king's foot pressing down on the cat's tail]
pages.scene: The king's foot pressing down on the cat's tail

pages.caption: With one terrific yell the cat sprang up and instantly changed into a tall man, who, fixing his angry eyes upon the King, said:
pages.description: [A cat transforming into an angry tall man]
pages.scene: A cat transforming into an angry tall man

pages.caption: "You shall marry the Princess because you have been able to break the enchantment, but I will have my revenge. You shall have a son, who will never be happy until he finds out that his nose is too long, and if you ever tell anyone what I have just said to you, you shall vanish away instantly, and no one shall ever see you or hear of you again."
pages.description: [The enchanter pointing a finger at the terrified king]
pages.scene: The enchanter pointing a finger at the terrified king

pages.caption: Though the King was horribly afraid of the enchanter, he could not help laughing at this threat.
pages.description: [The king stifling a laugh behind his hand]
pages.scene: The king stifling a laugh behind his hand

pages.caption: "If my son has such a long nose as that," he said to himself, "he must always see it or feel it; at least, if he is not blind or without hands."
pages.description: [The king smirking to himself]
pages.scene: The king smirking to himself

pages.caption: But, as the enchanter had vanished, he did not waste any more time in thinking, but went to seek the Princess, who very soon consented to marry him.
pages.description: [The king offering his hand to a beautiful princess]
pages.scene: The king offering his hand to a beautiful princess

pages.caption: But after all, they had not been married very long when the King died, and the Queen had nothing left to care for but her little son, who was called Hyacinth.
pages.description: [A queen cradling a baby with an enormous nose]
pages.scene: A queen cradling a baby with an enormous nose

pages.caption: The little Prince had large blue eyes, the prettiest eyes in the world, and a sweet little mouth, but, alas! his nose was so enormous that it covered half his face.
pages.description: [A baby with large blue eyes and a huge nose]
pages.scene: A baby with large blue eyes and a huge nose

pages.caption: The Queen was inconsolable when she saw this great nose, but her ladies assured her that it was not really as large as it looked; that it was a Roman nose, and you had only to open any history to see that every hero has a large nose.
pages.description: [The queen looking sadly at her baby]
pages.scene: The queen looking sadly at her baby

pages.caption: The Queen, who was devoted to her baby, was pleased with what they told her, and when she looked at Hyacinth again, his nose certainly did not seem to her _quite_ so large.
pages.description: [The queen smiling down at her child]
pages.scene: The queen smiling down at her child

pages.caption: The Prince was brought up with great care; and, as soon as he could speak, they told him all sorts of dreadful stories about people who had short noses.
pages.description: [Courtiers pulling their babies' noses]
pages.scene: Courtiers pulling their babies' noses

pages.caption: No one was allowed to come near him whose nose did not more or less resemble his own, and the courtiers, to get into favor with the Queen, took to pulling their babies' noses several times every day to make them grow long.
pages.description: [A room full of long-nosed courtiers bowing]
pages.scene: A room full of long-nosed courtiers bowing

pages.caption: When he grew sensible he learned history; and whenever any great prince or beautiful princess was spoken of, his teachers took care to tell him that they had long noses.
pages.description: [A young prince studying portraits of long-nosed kings]
pages.scene: A young prince studying portraits of long-nosed kings

pages.caption: His room was hung with pictures, all of people with very large noses; and the Prince grew up so convinced that a long nose was a great beauty, that he would not on any account have had his own a single inch shorter!
pages.description: [A bedroom walls covered in portraits of long-nosed people]
pages.scene: A bedroom walls covered in portraits of long-nosed people

pages.caption: When his twentieth birthday was passed the Queen thought it was time that he should be married, so she commanded that the portraits of several princesses should be brought for him to see, and among the others was a picture of the Dear Little Princess!
pages.description: [The queen presenting several princess portraits]
pages.scene: The queen presenting several princess portraits

pages.caption: Now, she was the daughter of a great king, and would some day possess several kingdoms herself; but Prince Hyacinth had not a thought to spare for anything of that sort, he was so much struck with her beauty.
pages.description: [A prince gazing at a portrait with rapturous eyes]
pages.scene: A prince gazing at a portrait with rapturous eyes

pages.caption: The Princess, whom he thought quite charming, had, however, a little saucy nose, which, in her face, was the prettiest thing possible.
pages.description: [A portrait of a beautiful princess with a tiny saucy nose]
pages.scene: A portrait of a beautiful princess with a tiny saucy nose

pages.caption: But it was a cause of great embarrassment to the courtiers, who had got into such a habit of laughing at little noses that they sometimes found themselves laughing at hers before they had time to think.
pages.description: [Two courtiers snickering behind their hands]
pages.scene: Two courtiers snickering behind their hands

pages.caption: But this did not do at all before the Prince, who quite failed to see the joke, and actually banished two of his courtiers who had dared to mention disrespectfully the Dear Little Princess's tiny nose!
pages.description: [The prince pointing angrily at banished courtiers]
pages.scene: The prince pointing angrily at banished courtiers

pages.caption: The others, taking warning from this, learned to think twice before they spoke, and one even went so far as to tell the Prince that, though it was quite true that no man could be anything unless he had a long nose, still, a woman's beauty was a different thing.
pages.description: [A courtier bowing and speaking wisely to the prince]
pages.scene: A courtier bowing and speaking wisely to the prince

pages.caption: And he knew a learned man who understood Greek and had read in some old manuscripts that the beautiful Cleopatra herself had a "tip-tilted" nose! The Prince made him a splendid present as a reward for this good news.
pages.description: [The prince presenting a gift to a bowing courtier]
pages.scene: The prince presenting a gift to a bowing courtier

pages.caption: And at once sent ambassadors to ask the Dear Little Princess in marriage. The King, her father, gave his consent.
pages.description: [Ambassadors riding out from the castle gates]
pages.scene: Ambassadors riding out from the castle gates

pages.caption: And Prince Hyacinth, who, in his anxiety to see the Princess, had gone three leagues to meet her was just advancing to kiss her hand.
pages.description: [The prince riding eagerly to meet a carriage]
pages.scene: The prince riding eagerly to meet a carriage

pages.caption: When, to the horror of all who stood by, the enchanter appeared as suddenly as a flash of lightning.
pages.description: [The enchanter appearing in a flash of lightning]
pages.scene: The enchanter appearing in a flash of lightning

pages.caption: And, snatching up the Dear Little Princess, whirled her away out of their sight!
pages.description: [A princess being snatched away into the sky]
pages.scene: A princess being snatched away into the sky

pages.caption: The Prince was left quite unconsolable, and declared that nothing should induce him to go back to his kingdom until he had found her again.
pages.description: [The prince standing alone, devastated]
pages.scene: The prince standing alone, devastated

pages.caption: And refusing to allow any of his courtiers to follow him, he mounted his horse and rode sadly away, letting the animal choose his own path.
pages.description: [A prince on horseback riding alone at dawn]
pages.scene: A prince on horseback riding alone at dawn

pages.caption: So it happened that he came presently to a great plain, across which he rode all day long without seeing a single house.
pages.description: [A vast empty plain stretching to the horizon]
pages.scene: A vast empty plain stretching to the horizon

pages.caption: And horse and rider were terribly hungry, when, as the night fell, the Prince caught sight of a light, which seemed to shine from a cavern.
pages.description: [An exhausted prince and horse at twilight]
pages.scene: An exhausted prince and horse at twilight

pages.caption: He rode up to it, and saw a little old woman, who appeared to be at least a hundred years old.
pages.description: [The prince peering into a glowing cavern]
pages.scene: The prince peering into a glowing cavern

pages.caption: She put on her spectacles to look at Prince Hyacinth, but it was quite a long time before she could fix them securely because her nose was so very short.
pages.description: [A tiny-nosed old fairy fumbling with spectacles]
pages.scene: A tiny-nosed old fairy fumbling with spectacles

pages.caption: The Prince and the Fairy (for that was who she was) had no sooner looked at one another than they went into fits of laughter, and cried at the same moment, "Oh, what a funny nose!"
pages.description: [The prince and fairy bursting into laughter]
pages.scene: The prince and fairy bursting into laughter

pages.caption: "Not so funny as your own," said Prince Hyacinth to the Fairy; "but, madam, I beg you to leave the consideration of our noses--such as they are--and to be good enough to give me something to eat, for I am starving, and so is my poor horse."
pages.description: [The prince gesturing to his own nose]
pages.scene: The prince gesturing to his own nose

pages.caption: "With all my heart," said the Fairy. "Though your nose is so ridiculous you are, nevertheless, the son of my best friend. I loved your father as if he had been my brother. Now _he_ had a very handsome nose!"
pages.description: [The fairy gesturing warmly toward her home]
pages.scene: The fairy gesturing warmly toward her home

pages.caption: "And pray what does mine lack?" said the Prince.
pages.description: [The prince raising an eyebrow]
pages.scene: The prince raising an eyebrow

pages.caption: "Oh! it doesn't _lack_ anything," replied the Fairy. "On the contrary quite, there is only too much of it. But never mind, one may be a very worthy man though his nose is too long.
pages.description: [The fairy examining the prince's nose critically]
pages.scene: The fairy examining the prince's nose critically

pages.caption: I was telling you that I was your father's friend; he often came to see me in the old times, and you must know that I was very pretty in those days; at least, he used to say so. I should like to tell you of a conversation we had the last time I ever saw him."
pages.description: [The fairy settling into a chair to reminisce]
pages.scene: The fairy settling into a chair to reminisce

pages.caption: "Indeed," said the Prince, "when I have supped it will give me the greatest pleasure to hear it; but consider, madam, I beg of you, that I have had nothing to eat to-day."
pages.description: [The prince gesturing impatiently toward the table]
pages.scene: The prince gesturing impatiently toward the table

pages.caption: "The poor boy is right," said the Fairy; "I was forgetting. Come in, then, and I will give you some supper, and while you are eating I can tell you my story in a very few words--for I don't like endless tales myself.
pages.description: [The fairy hurrying toward the kitchen]
pages.scene: The fairy hurrying toward the kitchen

pages.caption: Too long a tongue is worse than too long a nose, and I remember when I was young that I was so much admired for not being a great chatterer. They used to tell the Queen, my mother, that it was so.
pages.description: [The fairy lecturing with a raised finger]
pages.scene: The fairy lecturing with a raised finger

pages.caption: For though you see what I am now, I was the daughter of a great king. My father----"
pages.description: [The fairy gesturing grandly at herself]
pages.scene: The fairy gesturing grandly at herself

pages.caption: "Your father, I dare say, got something to eat when he was hungry!" interrupted the Prince.
pages.description: [The prince interrupting with a hungry glare]
pages.scene: The prince interrupting with a hungry glare

pages.caption: "Oh! certainly," answered the Fairy, "and you also shall have supper directly. I only just wanted to tell you----"
pages.description: [The fairy waving toward the supper table]
pages.scene: The fairy waving toward the supper table

pages.caption: "But I really cannot listen to anything until I have had something to eat," cried the Prince, who was getting quite angry; but then, remembering that he had better be polite as he much needed the Fairy's help, he added:
pages.description: [The prince growing visibly annoyed]
pages.scene: The prince growing visibly annoyed

pages.caption: "I know that in the pleasure of listening to you I should quite forget my own hunger; but my horse, who cannot hear you, must really be fed!"
pages.description: [The prince gesturing toward his horse outside]
pages.scene: The prince gesturing toward his horse outside

pages.caption: The Fairy was very much flattered by this compliment, and said, calling to her servants:
pages.description: [The fairy smiling with delight at the compliment]
pages.scene: The fairy smiling with delight at the compliment

pages.caption: "You shall not wait another minute, you are so polite, and in spite of the enormous size of your nose you are really very agreeable."
pages.description: [The fairy beckoning to her servants]
pages.scene: The fairy beckoning to her servants

pages.caption: "Plague take the old lady! How she does go on about my nose!" said the Prince to himself. "One would almost think that mine had taken all the extra length that hers lacks!
pages.description: [The prince scowling to himself]
pages.scene: The prince scowling to himself

pages.caption: If I were not so hungry I would soon have done with this chatterpie who thinks she talks very little! How stupid people are not to see their own faults!
pages.description: [The prince thinking angrily while waiting]
pages.scene: The prince thinking angrily while waiting

pages.caption: That comes of being a princess: she has been spoiled by flatterers, who have made her believe that she is quite a moderate talker!"
pages.description: [The prince smirking inwardly]
pages.scene: The prince smirking inwardly

pages.caption: Meanwhile the servants were putting the supper on the table, and the prince was much amused to hear the Fairy who asked them a thousand questions simply for the pleasure of hearing herself speak.
pages.description: [Servants laying dishes on a table while the fairy chatters]
pages.scene: Servants laying dishes on a table while the fairy chatters

pages.caption: Especially he noticed one maid who, no matter what was being said, always contrived to praise her mistress's wisdom.
pages.description: [A maid curtsying and praising her mistress]
pages.scene: A maid curtsying and praising her mistress

pages.caption: "Well!" he thought, as he ate his supper, "I'm very glad I came here. This just shows me how sensible I have been in never listening to flatterers.
pages.description: [The prince eating and reflecting with satisfaction]
pages.scene: The prince eating and reflecting with satisfaction

pages.caption: People of that sort praise us to our faces without shame, and hide our faults or change them into virtues. For my part I never will be taken in by them. I know my own defects, I hope."
pages.description: [The prince looking self-satisfied]
pages.scene: The prince looking self-satisfied

pages.caption: Poor Prince Hyacinth! He really believed what he said, and hadn't an idea that the people who had praised his nose were laughing at him, just as the Fairy's maid was laughing at her; for the Prince had seen her laugh slyly when she could do so without the Fairy's noticing her.
pages.description: [The prince oblivious while a maid smirks behind the fairy]
pages.scene: The prince oblivious while a maid smirks behind the fairy

pages.caption: However, he said nothing, and presently, when his hunger began to be appeased, the Fairy said: "My dear Prince, might I beg you to move a little more that way, for your nose casts such a shadow that I really cannot see what I have on my plate.
pages.description: [The fairy squinting at her plate in the shadow of the prince's nose]
pages.scene: The fairy squinting at her plate in the shadow of the prince's nose

pages.caption: Ah! thanks. Now let us speak of your father. When I went to his Court he was only a little boy, but that is forty years ago, and I have been in this desolate place ever since.
pages.description: [The fairy gesturing for the prince to move]
pages.scene: The fairy gesturing for the prince to move

pages.caption: Tell me what goes on nowadays; are the ladies as fond of amusement as ever? In my time one saw them at parties, theatres, balls, and promenades every day. Dear me! _what_ a long nose you have! I cannot get used to it!"
pages.description: [The fairy squinting up at the prince's nose]
pages.scene: The fairy squinting up at the prince's nose

pages.caption: "Really, madam," said the Prince, "I wish you would leave off mentioning my nose. It cannot matter to you what it is like. I am quite satisfied with it, and have no wish to have it shorter. One must take what is given one."
pages.description: [The prince raising his hand in exasperation]
pages.scene: The prince raising his hand in exasperation

pages.caption: "Now you are angry with me, my poor Hyacinth," said the Fairy, "and I assure you that I didn't mean to vex you; on the contrary, I wished to do you a service.
pages.description: [The fairy patting the prince's arm consolingly]
pages.scene: The fairy patting the prince's arm consolingly

pages.caption: However, though I really cannot help your nose being a shock to me, I will try not to say anything about it. I will even try to think that you have an ordinary nose. To tell the truth, it would make three reasonable ones."
pages.description: [The fairy holding up three fingers]
pages.scene: The fairy holding up three fingers

pages.caption: The Prince, who was no longer hungry, grew so impatient at the Fairy's continual remarks about his nose that at last he threw himself upon his horse and rode hastily away.
pages.description: [The prince leaping onto his horse in frustration]
pages.scene: The prince leaping onto his horse in frustration

pages.caption: But wherever he came in his journeyings he thought the people were mad, for they all talked of his nose, and yet he could not bring himself to admit that it was too long, he had been so used all his life to hear it called handsome.
pages.description: [The prince riding through towns while people stare and whisper]
pages.scene: The prince riding through towns while people stare and whisper

pages.caption: The old Fairy, who wished to make him happy, at last hit upon a plan.
pages.description: [The old fairy plotting in her cavern]
pages.scene: The old fairy plotting in her cavern

pages.caption: She shut the Dear Little Princess up in a palace of crystal, and put this palace down where the Prince would not fail to find it.
pages.description: [A princess trapped inside a shimmering crystal palace]
pages.scene: A princess trapped inside a shimmering crystal palace

pages.caption: His joy at seeing the Princess again was extreme, and he set to work with all his might to try to break her prison.
pages.description: [The prince discovering the crystal palace]
pages.scene: The prince discovering the crystal palace

pages.caption: But in spite of all his efforts he failed utterly.
pages.description: [The prince hammering uselessly against crystal walls]
pages.scene: The prince hammering uselessly against crystal walls

pages.caption: In despair he thought at least that he would try to get near enough to speak to the Dear Little Princess, who, on her part, stretched out her hand that he might kiss it.
pages.description: [The prince reaching through the crystal toward a hand]
pages.scene: The prince reaching through the crystal toward a hand

pages.caption: But turn which way he might, he never could raise it to his lips, for his long nose always prevented it.
pages.description: [The prince's nose blocking him from reaching the princess's hand]
pages.scene: The prince's nose blocking him from reaching the princess's hand

pages.caption: For the first time he realized how long it really was, and exclaimed: "Well, it must be admitted that my nose _is_ too long!"
pages.description: [The prince staring at his own nose in sudden realization]
pages.scene: The prince staring at his own nose in sudden realization

pages.caption: In an instant the crystal prison flew into a thousand splinters.
pages.description: [The crystal palace shattering into a thousand pieces]
pages.scene: The crystal palace shattering into a thousand pieces

pages.caption: And the old Fairy, taking the Dear Little Princess by the hand, said to the Prince: "Now, say if you are not very much obliged to me.
pages.description: [The fairy presenting the princess to the prince]
pages.scene: The fairy presenting the princess to the prince

pages.caption: Much good it was for me to talk to you about your nose! You would never have found out how extraordinary it was if it hadn't hindered you from doing what you wanted to.
pages.description: [The fairy gesturing at the prince's now-normal nose]
pages.scene: The fairy gesturing at the prince's now-normal nose

pages.caption: You see how self-love keeps us from knowing our own defects of mind and body. Our reason tries in vain to show them to us; we refuse to see them till we find them in the way of our interests."
pages.description: [The fairy speaking wisely]
pages.scene: The fairy speaking wisely

pages.caption: Prince Hyacinth, whose nose was now just like anyone's else, did not fail to profit by the lesson he had received.
pages.description: [The prince with a normal nose, kneeling before the princess]
pages.scene: The prince with a normal nose, kneeling before the princess

pages.caption: He married the Dear Little Princess, and they lived happily ever after.
pages.description: [A prince and princess dancing at their wedding]
pages.scene: A prince and princess dancing at their wedding
